title: Average AFL Player Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52 weeks. Includes the average AFL player salary, tax, super, and minimum wage.
salarySummary: Using a 38-hour week and 52 weeks, the average AFL player salary of $459,173 in 2024 converts to an hourly rate of about $232.50 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This is gross pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does casual loading affect the conversion?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. If you enter a base hourly rate, the timesheet on this site can add the loading automatically. The loading is paid instead of entitlements like sick leave and annual leave. The annual conversion uses the loaded rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate (currently 12%). It is not deducted from your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer pays an extra $7,200 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

Knowing how to turn an hourly wage into an annual figure helps you compare job offers, budget, and understand your worth. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees in Australia, the benchmark is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours every week, your annual gross pay is:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It gives you a base figure to work from. You can also calculate your fortnightly pay by doubling your weekly pay: $30 × 38 = $1,140 per week, so $2,280 per fortnight.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week, according to the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. This is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Many workers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher rates.

If you are covered by an award, your minimum hourly rate may be higher than the national minimum. The [pay guides](/blog) on this site can help you find the correct rate for your industry. Always check your award before relying on the national minimum.

## Example: The Average AFL Player Salary

To see how the conversion works at the top end, consider the average AFL player salary. According to data released by the AFL and reported by the average gross earnings for a listed player in 2024 was $459,173. This figure comes from total player payments of $296.3 million across 668 players. The average is projected to rise to about $519,000 by 2027 under the current collective bargaining agreement.

To find the equivalent hourly rate for a player earning $459,173 per year, assuming a 38-hour week (though AFL players’ actual hours vary greatly), we divide by 52 weeks and then by 38 hours:

$459,173 ÷ 52 = $8,830.25 per week
$8,830.25 ÷ 38 = $232.37 per hour

That is roughly $232 per hour before tax and super. For comparison, the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Australia were $2,083.70 per week as of May 2026, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. That converts to about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. The average AFL player salary is more than four times that.

## Understanding Your Fortnightly Pay

Your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. If you know your hourly rate, you can calculate your fortnightly gross: hourly rate × 38 hours × 2. For the average AFL player, that would be $232.37 × 38 × 2 = $17,660.12 per fortnight. For a minimum wage worker at $26.44 per hour, the fortnightly gross is $2,009.80.

Knowing your fortnightly amount is useful for budgeting, as many bills and rent are due fortnightly or monthly.

## Tax and Superannuation

Your annual gross salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates. For 2026–27, the tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income from $18,201 to $45,000 is taxed at 15%, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For an employee earning $459,173, the employer pays an extra $55,100.76 into super (capped at $32,499.60 if the cap applied only to the first $270,830? Actually, the cap applies to the first $270,830? The on-site reference says maximum contribution base $270,830. For earnings above that, no extra super is required. So for $459,173, the super is 12% of $270,830 = $32,499.60. The total super is $32,499.60. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how super works.

## Final Thoughts

Whether you are comparing a job offer that pays $30 per hour or you are curious about the average AFL player salary, the hourly-to-annual conversion is a useful tool. The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It gives you annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Use it as a starting point for negotiations and negotiations.

Remember that this is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Always consult your employer or a professional for your specific situation.
